title: Open Source Software
text: I build and maintain open-source tools that democratize access to economic data across Latin America. These packages are designed for researchers, analysts, and policymakers working on development economics, social policy evaluation, and quantitative research.

title: Open Source Software
section: Python Packages for Latin American Data
text:
Python Packages for Latin American Data
enahodata — Peru Household Survey Access GitHub · PyPI
Python package for simplified access to Peru’s National Household Survey (ENAHO) microdata. Download, process, and analyze data on poverty, employment, education, health, and household characteristics using pandas-compatible functions.

usebcrp — Central Reserve Bank of Peru API GitHub · PyPI
Python client for the Central Reserve Bank of Peru (BCRP) statistical API. Programmatic access to macroeconomic indicators, monetary policy data, and national accounts with pandas integration.

usecasen — Chile Socioeconomic Survey Tools GitHub · PyPI
Python tools for working with Chile’s National Socioeconomic Characterization Survey (CASEN). Facilitates multidimensional poverty analysis and social policy evaluation.

usebcch — Central Bank of Chile Database Client GitHub · PyPI
Python client for the Central Bank of Chile’s statistical database. Retrieve time series data on inflation, GDP, exchange rates, financial indicators, and external sector statistics.

title: Open Source Software
text:
Stata Packages
enahotools — ENAHO Data Processing for Stata GitHub
Stata package for processing and analyzing Peru’s National Household Survey (ENAHO). Automated data cleaning, variable labeling, and survey-weighted estimation commands.

title: Open Source Software
text:
Impact & Philosophy
These packages are part of my commitment to open science and data democratization. By lowering barriers to access public data, I aim to enable more rigorous research and evidence-based policymaking across Latin America.
All tools are open-source (MIT License), actively maintained, and built with reproducibility in mind.

title: Gold Price Shocks and Social Conflict
text:
NoteProject Status



This paper is currently under review. The preliminary version was presented at the LACEA 2024 Annual Meeting.

title: Gold Price Shocks and Social Conflict
text:
1. Overview
Does the boom in extractive industries fuel social unrest? Focusing on the Peruvian Amazon, we exploit exogenous variation in international gold prices combined with local mineral endowments to predict conflict probability at the district level.
We leverage data from three main sources: 1. Ombudsman’s Office (Defensoría del Pueblo): Monthly panel of social conflicts. 2. Sentinel-2 Satellite Imagery: To measure illegal mining deforestation. 3. MEF (SIAF): For local canon transfers analysis.

title: Gold Price Shocks and Social Conflict
text:
2. Methodology
We employ a Shift-Share Instrumental Variable (SSIV) strategy. The logic is to isolate the component of local economic growth driven purely by external price shocks.
\[
Z_{dt} = \text{Endowment}_d \times \log(\text{Price}_{t})
\]
Where \(Z_{dt}\) is the instrument for district \(d\) at time \(t\).

title: Gold Price Shocks and Social Conflict
text:
3. Implementation Code
Here is how we construct the instrument and run the core specification. Notice how we handle the spatial lag.

Stata (Estimation)Python (Spatial Viz)


* 1. Define the Shift-Share Instrument
gen shift_share_iv = gold_endowment * log(gold_price_int)

* 2. Main Specification (Fixed Effects)
reghdfe conflict_dummy shift_share_iv canon_transfers ///
    population_density, ///
    absorb(district_id year_month) ///
    vce(cluster district_id)

* 3. Export Results
outreg2 using "results/main_table.tex", replace tex


import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load District Data with Conflict Intensity
peru_map = gpd.read_file("data/peru_districts.geojson")

# Plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=(10, 10))
peru_map.plot(column='conflict_intensity', 
              ax=ax, 
              legend=True,
              cmap='OrRd',
              scheme='quantiles')

plt.title("Spatial Distribution of Social Conflicts (2023)")
plt.show()

title: Gold Price Shocks and Social Conflict
text:
4. Preliminary Results
The results suggest that a 10% increase in gold prices leads to a 2.5 percentage point increase in the probability of a socio-environmental conflict emerging in the subsequent quarter.

“The effect is driven primarily by competition for land rights rather than direct labor disputes.”

title: Maykol Medrano

I’m a Policy Data Scientist specializing in causal inference and machine learning for public policy evaluation. title: Illegal Mining Detection in Peruvian Amazon
text: This project combines remote sensing, machine learning, and spatial econometrics to detect and evaluate the impact of illegal gold mining in the Peruvian Amazon (Madre de Dios region).

title: Illegal Mining Detection in Peruvian Amazon
text:
Methods

Satellite imagery processing (Landsat 8, Sentinel-2)
Random Forest for land cover classification
Difference-in-Differences with spatial fixed effects
Geospatial buffer analysis for policy evaluation

title: Illegal Mining Detection in Peruvian Amazon
text:
Key Findings
Illegal mining expanded 15% annually between 2018-2023, with significant impacts on deforestation rates and mercury contamination in nearby water sources.

title: Illegal Mining Detection in Peruvian Amazon
text:
Policy Impact
Findings informed targeted enforcement strategies and environmental protection policies at the regional government level.

Full working paper and replication code available upon request.

title: Social Conflicts and Human Capital Accumulation
text: This study examines the causal effect of resource-related social conflicts on educational outcomes in Peru, using a difference-in-differences design with event-study specification.

title: Social Conflicts and Human Capital Accumulation
text: This study examines the causal effect of resource-related social conflicts on educational outcomes in Peru, using a difference-in-differences design with event-study specification.

title: Social Conflicts and Human Capital Accumulation
text:
Research Question
Do mining and hydrocarbon conflicts disrupt human capital accumulation in affected communities?

title: Social Conflicts and Human Capital Accumulation
text:
Methods

Event study with staggered treatment adoption
Callaway and Sant’Anna (2021) DID estimator
Shift-share instrumental variables for robustness
Administrative records from MINEDU and National Police

title: Social Conflicts and Human Capital Accumulation
text:
Preliminary Findings
Exposure to social conflicts reduces standardized test scores by 0.15 SD and increases dropout rates by 2.3 percentage points, with effects persisting for 3+ years.

title: Social Conflicts and Human Capital Accumulation
text:
Policy Implications
Results suggest the need for targeted educational interventions in conflict-affected areas and improved conflict prevention mechanisms in extractive zones.

Master’s thesis in progress. Draft available Q2 2025.
